verdict.label: BUY / SELECTIVE — 30Y Breaks Below 5.0%; AI Capex Supercycle Confirmed
verdict.rationale_short: SPX closed at a new record (7,580.06) for the ninth consecutive winning week. DELL surged 33% on AI server revenue +757% YoY and a $51.3B backlog — the most definitive AI capex validation in the series. The 30Y closed at 4.97%, the first close below 5.0% since May 14, resolving the series' most critical rate trigger. VIX 15.32 (-2.67%) continues declining. Conviction stays at medium — not high — because the Iran MoU remains unsigned (weekend binary risk), nine consecutive winning weeks requires procyclical discipline, and Warsh FOMC June 16-17 with PCE at 3.8% is an unresolved structural gate.

bear_case: Counter-argument: nine consecutive winning weeks in an environment where April PCE headline stands at 3.8% YoY — the highest since May 2023 — means the market has now fully priced in every positive binary: AI capex acceleration (DELL +33%), Iran ceasefire (still unsigned), rate normalization (30Y at 4.97%), and Warsh FOMC restraint. The 30Y closing at 4.97% is being read as a regime-clearing event; but month-end bond buying mechanically suppresses yields on the last trading day of the month, and the 5-day average remains above 5.00% — one close below does not change the structural rate environment that Warsh's 8-4 hawkish committee controls. If Warsh hikes 25bps on June 17, the 30Y spikes back toward 5.20-5.30%, the entire BUY framework unwinds simultaneously, and the market will be at nine-week record highs with no defensive cushion. The DELL +33% single-session surge creates forced-covering crowding risk across AI infrastructure names: every desk that was underweight or short the sector is now covering at a single price level, which historically marks the exhaustion of a move, not the beginning of the next leg. Invalidation level: if SPX loses 7,460 on a daily close and 30Y closes above 5.10%, the BUY framework converts to Step Aside immediately. If Warsh raises rates June 17, exit all longs simultaneously.
